- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak predictions to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — model should not undershoot the true mean.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of price decline after spike), forecast should not continue the trend beyond 1–2 days.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially in 30d forecasts) are common — cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- If sentiment is volatile or near-zero, forecast should be closer to recent 7–14 day average, not extreme 30d trend.  
- When true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was high — if so, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with sentiment decay.  
- If sentiment is consistently low and price is trending up, model should not overreact — cap upward momentum at 1.2x recent 14-day average.
